operating_notes.text: Company borrowed ₹65 Cr unsecured from promoter-group Ultramarine & Pigments at 10% p.a. for 3 years, executed April 30, 2026.
Group current liabilities exceed current assets by ₹74,212 lakhs at 30 June 2026, mainly capex at TCL Specialties LLC, USA.
TCL Specialties LLC is raising USD 130-180 million of debt, with financing expected to be completed by October 2026.
Windmill sale: four windmills of 3.2 MW on 11.42 acres in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, to TN Oxygen Private Limited for ₹10.35 Cr; windmill revenue was ₹158 lakhs, 0.11% of revenue.
Dahej PAn reactor achieved 95% capacity utilisation in Q1FY27.
US project estimated cost revised to approximately US$340 million including working capital and ramp-up costs.
OOSB Malaysia reported positive EBITDA in Q1FY27 on operational optimisation and cost control.
ICRA: total PAN capacity ~1,72,000 TPA including Dahej phase 1; second-largest PAN player in India.
ICRA: FY27 principal repayments ~₹169.92 Cr and FY28 ~₹217.79 Cr; unencumbered cash ~₹63.99 Cr at March 31, 2026.
ICRA: anti-dumping duty on PAN imports from China and Korea extended for five years from August 06, 2026.
GST show cause notice from Central GST Audit Commissionerate, Vadodara, disallowing ₹33.47 lakh of ITC on stock difference for April 2020 to March 2024; interest and penalty to be ascertained.
Thirumalai holds 41,98,837 shares (14.38%) of Ultramarine & Pigments as promoter and approved selling up to 14,60,000 shares (5%) within 7 working days; BSE close on 28.08.2026 was ₹410.70.
Thirumalai approved selling up to 9,50,000 Ultramarine & Pigments shares (3.25% of capital) in the open market; it would then hold 27,38,837 shares (9.38%); NSE close on 30.09.2026 was ₹418.50.

GST show cause notice under Section 73 of the CGST Act from the Assistant Commissioner, Ranipet (Sipcot), for AY2022-23, seeking ₹13.52 lakh including interest and penalty on alleged exempt-turnover discrepancies and excess ITC; company say
Received Customs audit observation for ₹24.52 lakhs plus interest and penalty regarding RoDTEP benefits on DFIA exports for 2024-2026.

timeline.summary: On 30 April 2026 Thirumalai Chemicals signed a ₹65 Cr unsecured 3-year loan agreement with promoter-group Ultramarine & Pigments at 10% p.a.
On May 13, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval to secure loan facilities up to USD 140 million through subsidiary asset and share pledges.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹424.25 Cr (-18.9% YoY), net loss ₹28 Cr (against a loss of ₹14.06 Cr a year earlier).
On May 30, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals filed its statement of deviation or variation in fund utilization for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
On July 31, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals disclosed a GST show cause notice of ₹22.93 Cr for FY23 from the Commercial Tax Department, Ranipet.
Q1FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹546.67 Cr (+21.5% YoY), net loss ₹43.67 Cr (against a loss of ₹59.96 Cr a year earlier).
Q1FY27 investor presentation: consolidated revenue ₹547 Cr (+22% YoY), EBITDA ₹36 Cr vs -₹25 Cr, net loss ₹44 Cr; US project cost revised to ~US$340 mn with commissioning targeted December 2026.
Thirumalai Chemicals Limited’s 53rd AGM held on August 07, 2026, with 74 shareholders (26 promoters, 48 public) via video conference.

On August 13, 2026, ICRA downgraded Thirumalai Chemicals' long-term rating to [ICRA]BBB (Negative) from [ICRA]BBB+ (Negative) and short-term to [ICRA]A3+ from [ICRA]A2, citing the US project cost rise to USD 340 million and stretched liquidity.

On August 18, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals received a GST show cause notice from the Central GST Audit Commissionerate, Vadodara, for ₹33.47 lakh of ITC on stock difference for April 2020 to March 2024; the company called the demand erroneous.
On August 29, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals announced the resignation of Walker Chandiok & Co LLP as statutory auditor of material subsidiary TCL Intermediates.

On August 30, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals' Fund Raising Committee approved the sale of up to 14,60,000 Ultramarine & Pigments shares (5% of its capital) from its 14.38% promoter holding, within 7 working days.

On September 30, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals' Fund Raising Committee approved selling up to 9,50,000 Ultramarine & Pigments shares (3.25% of its capital) in the open market, leaving it 27,38,837 shares or 9.38%.

On September 29, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals received a GST show cause notice under Section 73 of the CGST Act from the Assistant Commissioner, Ranipet (Sipcot), for AY2022-23, seeking ₹13.52 lakh including interest and penalty on alleged exempt-turnover discrepancies and excess ITC; the company called the demand erroneous, citing its SEZ unit.
On October 22, 2026, Thirumalai Chemicals disclosed a Customs audit observation seeking ₹0.25 Cr plus interest and penalty for alleged ineligible RoDTEP benefits on DFIA exports.
